extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark designed to systematically analyze the mathematical reasoning capabilities of state-of-the-art models in visually complex scenarios. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The benchmark covers seven types of mathematical reasoning: algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric commonsense, scientific, and statistical reasoning. It includes five primary tasks: figure question answering (FQA), geometry problem solving (GPS), math word problem (MWP), textbook question answering (TQA), and visual question answering (VQA). The dataset encompasses diverse visual contexts such as natural images, geometry diagrams, abstract scenes, synthetic scenes, charts, plots, and tables. The benchmark evaluates models' abilities in fine-grained visual understanding, compositional reasoning, and mathematical reasoning in visually rich real-world tasks.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MATHVISTA: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.02255.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The data collection process involved: 1) Reviewing over 70 datasets to select 19 publicly available ones that contain math-related instances. 2) Automatically selecting examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning using heuristic rules based on quantity words. 3) Manually labeling these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning. 4) Creating three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) to address gaps in logical reasoning on puzzle test figures, statistical reasoning on functional plots, and scientific reasoning on academic paper figures. 5) Ensuring data quality through a rigorous review process with high inter-annotation consistency (99.2%).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data sources include 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets. The existing datasets include MathQA datasets (e.g., Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo, CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP, SciBench, TheoremQA) and general VQA datasets (e.g., ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, VQA-AS). The newly created datasets include IQTest (228 examples), FunctionQA (400 examples), and PaperQA (107 examples).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The preprocessing steps included: 1) Automatic selection of examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning using heuristic rules based on quantity words. 2) Manual labeling to verify mathematical reasoning involvement. 3) Limiting each source dataset to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. 4) For newly created datasets, manual annotation by graduate students in STEM fields followed by a rigorous review process. 5) Annotating examples with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created through a multi-step process: 1) For existing datasets, metadata such as question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context were extracted from source datasets. 2) For newly created datasets, questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. 3) A two-step annotation process was used: initial independent annotation by three reviewers followed by discussion to resolve discrepancies. 4) Mathematical reasoning categories were manually labeled for 1,000 examples to verify the accuracy of automatic annotations. 5) Examples were annotated with seven different types of mathematical reasoning abilities.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tools were developed for manual labeling and verification processes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process achieved high inter-annotation consistency with a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 for mathematical reasoning labeling. Among 736 newly collected questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in annotated answers, which were resolved through discussion. The accuracy of automatic annotation for mathematical reasoning categories was verified by comparing with human annotations, showing 94.1% exact match and 98.79% individual label match.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: The dataset contains 6,141 examples with varying annotation levels. 85.6% of examples (5,261) have annotations, while 12.0% (736) are newly annotated examples. The annotations include metadata such as question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and mathematical reasoning types.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were graduate students in STEM fields with expertise in mathematical reasoning and visual understanding. The annotation team included individuals with backgrounds in computer science, mathematics, and related disciplines.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: EasyOCR for text extraction from images, and custom annotation tools for manual labeling and verification processes.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is maintained through an online evaluation platform. The test set answers are not publicly released to prevent data contamination. The dataset will be updated based on community feedback and new model developments.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not contain personal sensitive information as it focuses on mathematical reasoning tasks rather than personal data collection.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance AI capabilities in mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, which has applications in educational tools, scientific analysis, and general-purpose AI assistants. The benchmark helps identify limitations in current models and guides future research directions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases inherent in the source datasets, particularly in terms of visual context representation and mathematical reasoning types. The dataset includes examples from diverse sources but may not be fully representative of all possible mathematical reasoning scenarios or visual contexts.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: 1) Limited coverage of certain types of mathematical problems and visual contexts. 2) Heterogeneous annotation formats from different source datasets. 3) Potential data noise from source datasets. 4) Focus on specific domains like science and college-level math requiring labor-intensive data collection. 5) The dataset may not fully capture the complexity of real-world mathematical reasoning tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training, testing, and validation of foundation models in mathematical reasoning within visual contexts. It serves as a benchmark for evaluating model performance across different mathematical reasoning types and visual contexts. The dataset is particularly useful for developing models capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks.
